hero.lead: The practical programme for leaders and teams responsible for AI, built on real regulatory frameworks and delivered by governance practitioners, not academic theorists. Then an advisory practice that takes governance from policy to practice.

tracks.title: Three tracks. One governance language.
tracks.lead: Each track gives participants what they need for their role, so when governance decisions surface, everyone across the organisation speaks the same language.

items.name: Executive intensive
items.description: A concentrated programme for boards, the C-suite and senior leadership: AI governance strategy, the regulatory landscape, board-level oversight and how to read a governance health score.
items.alt: Two people reviewing a decision together

items.name: Practitioner programme
items.description: A two-day deep dive for governance, risk, compliance, legal and technology teams: EU AI Act implementation, ISO 42001 requirements, risk assessment methodology and evidence compilation.
items.alt: Analytics dashboard with charts and metrics

items.name: AI team workshop
items.description: A one-day workshop for product managers, data scientists and AI engineers: DevSecOps guardrails, LLM prompt-injection defence, agentic autonomy limits and bias testing in training pipelines.
items.audience: ML engineers · Data scientists · Product · AI architects
items.alt: Close-up of code on a dark terminal screen

curriculum.title: What you'll actually learn.
curriculum.lead: Sixteen modules taught through real governance scenarios, not abstract theory. Participants leave with knowledge they use the next day.

modules.title: AI Governance Fundamentals
modules.body: Definitions, core principles and the AI lifecycle.

modules.title: EU AI Act in Practice
modules.body: Annex III classification, conformity and Article 27 FRIA.

modules.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023
modules.body: Designing and certifying an AI Management System.

modules.title: NIST AI RMF 1.0
modules.body: Operationalising GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE.

modules.title: AI Risk Management
modules.body: Scoring probabilistic systems vs. deterministic code.

modules.title: AI Lifecycle Governance
modules.body: From prototype to production monitoring and retirement.

modules.title: Agentic AI & Autonomous Systems
modules.body: Tool use, runtime boundaries and kill-switches.

modules.title: UAE & GCC Regulatory Suite
modules.body: DIFC Regulation 10, UAE PDPL and ADGM FSRA mandates.

modules.title: Governance Operating Models
modules.body: RACI matrices, AI ethics committees and role definition.

modules.title: Board & C-Suite Reporting
modules.body: Metrics that convey real risk without technical jargon.

modules.title: Third-Party AI & Supply Chain
modules.body: Auditing SaaS vendors, foundation models and external APIs.

modules.title: LLM Evaluation & Red Teaming
modules.body: Stress-testing, hallucination detection and jailbreak prevention.

modules.title: Data Governance for AI
modules.body: Training data provenance, copyright and synthetic data validation.

modules.title: Maturity & Continuous Improvement
modules.body: Progressing from Level 1 Emerging to Level 5 Adaptive.

outcomes.title: What your team leaves with.
items: A shared governance vocabulary across teams
A deep understanding of the regulations that apply
The ability to assess AI systems for risk and compliance
Practical knowledge of policy and control design
Internal champions to drive governance adoption
A governance baseline to measure progress

practice.title: Strategy. Framework. Implementation. Assurance.
practice.lead: Niticore Advisory goes beyond strategy decks. Certified practitioners design governance that actually gets implemented, then configure it straight into the platform so it sticks.

areas.name: Strategy
areas.title: Build the strategy.
areas.body: Define the vision, priorities and operating model for AI governance. Align stakeholders from the board to the build team before a single policy is written.
points: AI governance vision, risk appetite and principles
Regulatory exposure mapped across every operating region
Governance structure, AI committee charter and RACI roles

areas.name: Framework
areas.title: Design the framework.
areas.body: Bespoke frameworks, policies and controls for your sector, scale and regulatory context. Not a generic template.
points: Policy suites for acceptable use, model validation and procurement
Control libraries harmonised across ISO 42001, EU AI Act, NIST and UAE mandates
Custom risk classification rubrics and assessment criteria

areas.name: Implementation
areas.title: Operationalise across your organisation.
areas.body: Turn the framework into daily practice, embedded in workflows, tools and teams. This is where most governance programmes stall.
points: Niticore workflows, approval gates and CI/CD and MLOps integrations
Governance checkpoints inside JIRA, ServiceNow and GitHub
Change management, champion training and handover

areas.name: Assurance
areas.title: Validate and continuously improve.
areas.body: Independent review of your governance posture against frameworks, regulations and your own standards. An ongoing assurance relationship, not a one-off audit.
points: Formal gap analyses and external audit dry runs
Preparation for accredited ISO/IEC 42001 certification audits
Regulatory intelligence and quarterly executive posture reviews

engage.title: Three ways to start.
engage.lead: Not every organisation needs the same commitment. Choose the engagement that fits where you are.

models.name: Discovery Workshop
models.outcome: Executive briefing, a regulatory heat map and your top 5 immediate governance gaps.

models.name: Governance Sprint
models.outcome: Framework designed, policies authored, initial AI portfolio registered on Niticore and team trained.

models.name: Ongoing Advisory Retainer
models.outcome: Continuous regulatory updates, quarterly audits, incident response guidance and board-ready reporting support.

cta.title: We don't just help you comply. We help you build the capability.
cta.lead: Talk to a governance expert about what your organisation needs to move from documentation to durable governance.
